facts.text: In 1798, settlers Valentine Cunningham and Robert Glenn built the first gristmill on Wolf Creek, sparking the settlement that would become Grove City.
Grove City officially incorporated on January 1, 1883, adopting its current name after previously being called Pine Grove.
Pine Grove Academy, founded in 1858, evolved into Grove City College, a private liberal‑arts institution today.
In the 19th century, Grove City became an industrial hub, producing locomotive engines, carriages, gas engines, foundry goods, and motor trucks.
The Pittsburgh, Shenango and Lake Erie Railroad extended to the area in 1872, connecting Grove City to the regional rail network.
Early 1800s saw Cunningham build a sawmill and schoolhouse, while Robert Moore developed Slabtown with a sawmill and small businesses.
